page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the e2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. This server does not include any bundled GPUs or local storage, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance primarily in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng CPU tests, both single-core and multi-core performance are rated as weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks register in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression performance are poor, placing in the bottom 10%. Geekbench scores reflect a similar trend, with single-core and multi-core results categorized as poor. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in text generation for small 135M LLM models, achieving 104.71 tokens per second, though prompt processing remains weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-4 offers a resource-dense, entry-level hardware profile suitable for utility computing where high-performance throughput is not a primary requirement. Given the weak to poor benchmark results in database operations, software compilation, and cryptography, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Appropriate applications include basic web serving, small-scale Redis deployments, development environments, and low-intensity background tasks that benefit from a dedicated CPU allocation without requiring high computational velocity.
